doc.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023

title: Self-plagiarism and closing thanks
summary: Rowe thanks her, then asks about plagiarizing herself; Bailey says writing more hones one's voice, and they say goodbye.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Okay. Well this has been a marvelous conversation. I want to thank you for your time.
Sure thank you, it was super fun. Great questions.
And good luck with your projects. I left out one question I had about your composing and that is do you ever plagiarize yourself?

Ha! I think everybody does. Yeah. I mean when you hear anybody and you listen to a bunch of their music in a row you hear techniques and — what’s the word — tendencies. Yeah. Everybody has their tendencies. But I think that’s why you should write more because the more you write it hones that, your voice as a composer. I think it’s good.
Terrific. Thanks for your time, Sheryl.
Yeah thank you. I look forward to checking this out when it’s done and we’ll share it around. It was great. Thank you so much. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
